# Audio and media you can replace

*Generated by `python -m alien_remake --media-doc`. Do not edit by hand: `alien_remake.media` is the source, and a test fails if this file falls behind it.*

Every file the game will use in place of its own, where to put it, and what it has to be. Nothing here changes how the game plays or where anything sits on screen - see the last section.

## Where files go

Paths below are relative to an **asset root**. These are searched in order and the first hit wins, so a file in an earlier root beats the derived one without replacing it:

1. `$ALIEN_REMAKE_ASSETS`, if you have set it
2. `out/` in the current directory
3. `out/` beside the checkout (or the frozen executable)
4. your per-user data directory, next to `settings.toml`

Run `python -m alien_remake --media` to see those resolved to real paths on your own machine, and which files it can currently find. They are deliberately not written out here: they differ per machine, and a document that hard-codes one person's home directory is a document that misleads everybody else.

The point of the search order is that you never have to overwrite what the extractor produced - put your own work in an earlier root and delete it to get the original back.

## Derived from your own disk

**File format:** whatever the extractor produces - see `make it with` below

| put it here | what it replaces |
|---|---|
| `charset.bin` | the game's own glyphs and sprites - put a different charset at glyphs/charset.bin and it is used instead - this derived file stays where it is, so you keep what came off your own disk |
| `intro.wav` | the SID intro tune - drop your own intro.wav in a root ahead of out/ and it plays instead of the emulated SID - any length, it loops as the original does |
| `basic.bin` | the BASIC ROM the opening's garbled victim name is read out of (make it with: `capture $A000-$BFFF, or use a VICE basic-901226-01.bin`) |
| `chargen.bin` | the C64 character generator, for text the game's own charset lacks (make it with: `capture $D000-$DFFF from the chargen ROM`) |
| `Alien (USA, Europe)_files/MENU1.prg` | the loader's BASIC, source of the on-screen instructions (make it with: `python -m alientools extract "Alien (USA, Europe).nib" --out out/`) |

## The character set

**File format:** an 8192-byte $2000-$3FFF charset region dump, or a whole ALIEN .prg to take the region from

| put it here | what it replaces |
|---|---|
| `glyphs/charset.bin` | the 8K $2000-$3FFF charset region, or a whole ALIEN prg to take it from; drawn in place of the game's own letters and map tiles |

## Deck plans

**File format:** PNG, 240x144 (30 columns x 18 rows of 8x8 cells); anything larger is scaled down to that

| put it here | what it replaces |
|---|---|
| `map/upper.png` | the Upper Deck plan; 240x144, drawn in place of the deck the game builds from its own screen codes |
| `map/middle.png` | the Middle Deck plan; 240x144, drawn in place of the deck the game builds from its own screen codes |
| `map/lower.png` | the Lower Deck plan; 240x144, drawn in place of the deck the game builds from its own screen codes |

## The game's own sound effects

**File format:** WAV. 44100 Hz is the mixer's rate, so that is what avoids a resample; 16-bit, mono or stereo. Stereo only opens the mixer in stereo when GAME AUDIO is 'sampled'

| put it here | what it replaces |
|---|---|
| `sounds/heartbeat.wav  or  sounds/heartbeat/*.wav` | the selected crew member's heartbeat - it beats faster as their composure drops |
| `sounds/grille.wav  or  sounds/grille/*.wav` | a duct grille being opened or shut |
| `sounds/movement.wav  or  sounds/movement/*.wav` | the blip as a crew member arrives in a room |
| `sounds/tracker_alarm.wav  or  sounds/tracker_alarm/*.wav` | the motion tracker's ping when the Alien is detected |
| `sounds/airlock.wav  or  sounds/airlock/*.wav` | an airlock cycling, and the crack of one being blown |
| `sounds/attack_alert.wav  or  sounds/attack_alert/*.wav` | the siren while the Alien is attacking - only for the crew member you are watching |

## Interface sounds (not in the original)

**File format:** WAV, 44100 Hz 16-bit, mono or stereo. A cue may be a folder of several files, and one is picked at random

| put it here | what it replaces |
|---|---|
| `sounds/menu_move.wav  or  sounds/menu_move/*.wav` | the cursor moving to another row |
| `sounds/menu_change.wav  or  sounds/menu_change/*.wav` | an option's value changing |
| `sounds/menu_select.wav  or  sounds/menu_select/*.wav` | picking a different crew member |
| `sounds/screen_enter.wav  or  sounds/screen_enter/*.wav` | arriving on a new screen |
| `sounds/crt_warmup.wav  or  sounds/crt_warmup/*.wav` | the tube warming up, once, at the first frame drawn |

## Not replaceable

- **layouts** - deliberately, not for want of a mechanism: the owner's ruling is that the layout stays the original's and only the art inside it is yours to change, so nothing here can move a thing or resize it

## What replacing a file cannot do

Supplying a file changes a picture or a sound. It cannot move anything, resize anything, or change a rule: every drawn override is scaled to a size taken from the machine (a hardware sprite is 24x21, the map field is 240x144), and nothing reads a dimension off your file. That is the owner's ruling on D4, and DEC-041 records it.

Two exceptions run the other way, and they are there to *protect* the game rather than to limit you. The selected crew member's marker pulses on the ROM's own heartbeat, and the marker portrait is black in a room and white in a duct. Those colours are telling the player something, so on those two the game washes its colour over your art at half strength instead of dropping it - you keep the picture, and the player keeps the signal.
